nodes.name: Harvard's review of its Epstein ties (May 2020)
nodes.note: $9.1M in gifts, 1998-2008, none accepted after the conviction; $6.5M (2003) helped create the Program for Evolutionary Dynamics; Visiting Fellow in 2005 though he lacked the usual qualifications; more than 40 visits to the programme's offices 2010-18, with key cards, the passcode and a key to "Jeffrey's Office"; after the conviction he helped steer another donor's gift, which development officers knew of. $200,937 unspent went to two survivor charities.

nodes.name: Program for Evolutionary Dynamics (Harvard)
nodes.note: Created with Epstein's $6.5M gift (2003), directed by Martin Nowak. Gave Epstein access cards, the office passcode and a key to an office it called "Jeffrey's Office" before 2017 (Harvard review).

nodes.name: Stephen Kosslyn
nodes.note: Harvard psychology chair. Received $200,000 from Epstein 1998-2002 and recommended him as a Visiting Fellow in 2005 (Harvard review).

nodes.name: MIT's Goodwin Procter report (Jan 2020)
nodes.note: $850,000 in ten gifts 2002-17, nine after the conviction: $525,000 to the Media Lab, $225,000 to Seth Lloyd, $100,000 for Marvin Minsky (2002). Three vice presidents learned of his record in 2013 and approved later gifts under an informal framework; nine campus visits 2013-17 driven by Ito or Lloyd; President Reif did not know.

nodes.name: MIT vice presidents Morgan, Newton and Ruiz
nodes.note: R. Gregory Morgan, Jeffrey Newton and Israel Ruiz learned in 2013 of the Media Lab gifts and his sex-offence record and approved later gifts under an informal framework they set up (Goodwin Procter report).

nodes.name: Forbes (contributor network)
nodes.note: Ran a 2013 contributor piece praising Epstein as a "science funder"; removed in 2019 for failing editorial standards after a New York Times inquiry.

nodes.name: National Review Online
nodes.note: Ran a 2013 piece under the byline of Christina Galbraith, who worked as Epstein's publicist; removed in 2019.

nodes.name: HuffPost (contributor network)
nodes.note: Ran a 2017 contributor piece praising his work with scientists; removed in 2019 at the author's request.

nodes.name: Drew Hendricks
nodes.note: Forbes contributor. The New York Times reported that a PR firm supplied his 2013 piece on Epstein and that he was paid $600 to post it under his name.

nodes.name: Christina Galbraith
nodes.note: Worked as a publicist for Epstein (New York Times); a 2013 National Review piece under her byline praised him.
